title: Resolution of a nodal curve over a smooth normal-crossings pair
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field. Let $Y$ be a smooth integral finite-type $F$-scheme. Let $T\subset Y$ be a reduced effective Cartier divisor with strict normal crossings. This means that its finitely many irreducible components are smooth and every intersection of $r$ distinct components is empty or smooth of codimension $r$ in $Y$; the empty divisor is allowed. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a projective flat finitely presented morphism with $X$ integral, with smooth geometrically integral generic fibre, and with nonempty connected one-dimensional geometric fibres having at worst ordinary double points. Assume $f$ is smooth over $Y\setminus T$. Let $D\subset X$ be an effective Cartier divisor, finite etale over $Y$ and contained in the relative smooth locus. Then there is a proper birational morphism $r:\widetilde X\to X$ with $\widetilde X$ integral and smooth over $F$ such that $(r^{-1}(|D|\cup f^{-1}|T|))_{\mathrm{red}}$ is a strict normal crossings divisor. Birational means that $r$ induces an isomorphism on dense open subschemes. An effective Cartier divisor is locally cut out by one non-zero-divisor. An ordinary double point has completed geometric fibre ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$.

Conventions for the notions used here: smoothness [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]; integrality [def-pc-integral-scheme]; finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; projectivity [def-kun-projective]; flatness [def-weil-flat-morphism]; finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]; geometric integrality, connectedness and reducedness [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]; etaleness [def-weil-etale-morphism]; closed subschemes [def-weil-closed-immersion]; reduction [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]; properness [def-weil-proper-morphism].

The local form uv=a, with a supported on the normal-crossings boundary, is the nodal-pair case. Full Vidal source WANTED. Only properness of the modification is asserted; it holds because the source's modifications are projective in the projective-bundle sense.

proof.text: The projective morphism $f$ is proper by [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper], hence finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Composing with $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ using [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] shows that $X$ is finite type over $F$. The spectrum of a field is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and the unit ideal); apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] first to $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}F$, then to $f$, to obtain that $Y$ and $X$ are Noetherian.

Apply [lem-trf-snc-divisorial-log-chart] to $(Y,T)$. Its hypotheses are exactly the given smoothness, finite type, reduced Cartier condition and smooth codimension-$r$ intersections. It identifies the divisorial characteristic monoid with $\mathbf N^r$ at an $r$-fold intersection and proves that $(Y,|T|)$ is log regular, including when $T$ is empty.

Put $B=|D|\cup f^{-1}|T|$. Apply [lem-trf-nodal-log-regularity] with the Noetherian schemes of step 1 and the log regular base of step 2. Properness was checked in step 1; flatness, finite presentation, connected one-dimensional nodal geometric fibres, and smoothness off $T$ are the given hypotheses. The marked divisor is etale over $Y$ and lies in the relative smooth locus as required; finite etaleness is stronger than the etaleness used here. Therefore $B$ is nowhere dense and $(X,B)$ is log regular. This step does not assume that the two local branches of a node are globally separate.

Use [lem-trf-log-regular-desingularization] for the integral finite-type $F$-scheme $X$ and its log regular boundary $B$. Obtain a proper $F$-morphism $p:X_1\to X$, integral regular finite-type $X_1$, and the normal crossings Cartier divisor $B_1=(p^{-1}B)_{\rm red}$. The map is an isomorphism over $U=X\setminus B$, with dense inverse image of $U$. At this point the boundary is only normal crossings; its irreducible components may still have self-intersections.

Apply [lem-trf-normal-crossings-strictification] to $(X_1,B_1)$. Its hypotheses require regularity and normal crossings, both supplied in step 4, and finite type over the same algebraically closed field $F$. It yields a proper $q:\widetilde X\to X_1$, with $\widetilde X$ integral and smooth over $F$, and $B_2=(q^{-1}B_1)_{\rm red}$ strict normal crossings in the smooth-intersection sense stated in the item. The isomorphism over $X_1\setminus|B_1|$ includes the inverse image of $U$.

Set $r=p\circ q$. It is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]. Both maps are isomorphisms over the nonempty dense open $U=X\setminus B$ (nonemptiness follows from step 3 and the integrality of $X$); their composite is an isomorphism there. Its inverse image is a nonempty open of the integral scheme $\widetilde X$, hence is dense, so this is birational in the required sense. Finally, inverse images of sets compose and reduction does not change a closed subset [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction], so $|q^{-1}B_1|=q^{-1}p^{-1}B=r^{-1}B$. The corresponding reduced closed subschemes are therefore equal, giving $(r^{-1}(|D|\cup f^{-1}|T|))_{\rm red}=B_2$, the strict normal crossings divisor of step 5.

source.place: Conclusion by composition and equality of reduced closed subschemes with the same support.

split_report.summary: Kept the full statement unchanged. Split the nodal-pair modification into divisorial log charts on the base, log regularity of the marked nodal curve, regular modification of a log regular pair, and strictification of its normal crossings boundary. Used the available ILO proofs rather than the unavailable Vidal source. Kept regular versus smooth and normal versus strict normal crossings distinct; no global branch separation was assumed. Created one definition and four statement-only geometric lemmas; the properness/finite-type/composition facts reuse existing nodes.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q83-2af2ddddb (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery against ILO Gabber VI 1.1-1.9 (including the proof of Prop 1.9), VIII 3.4.1-3.4.10, VIII 4.1-4.1.8 with Rem 4.2.2, X Lemma 2.2 (pp.149-150), and Stacks 0B8X, 0BIA and 0CBY. The item statement is unchanged and not weakened. It is not a target, so no base-change morphism or coefficient category is involved. Its six steps check out. (1) Projective implies proper and of finite type, the composite is of finite type, and X and Y are Noetherian; each cited statement says this. (2) The SNC chart lemma's hypotheses are exactly the item's hypotheses on (Y,T). (3) The nodal lemma's hypotheses were checked one by one. It matches VI 1.9 and adds only hypotheses (connected, nonempty, finitely presented, Noetherian). (4) Kato-Niziol desingularization by saturated log blow-ups (VIII 3.4.6(i), 3.4.9, VI 1.7) needs no characteristic-zero input. (5) Strictification is VIII 4.1.6-4.1.8; regular becomes smooth by 0B8X because F is perfect. Its normal-crossings input has the same definition as the output of (4). (6) Proper composition holds. Birationality uses the nonempty dense open U=X\B. The boundary equality uses only that reduction is the identity on underlying sets. Tests: empty T and D; T empty forcing f smooth; uv=t, uv=t^n and uv=t1t2. For the chart lemma: in the UFD strict local ring, the boundary-unit monoid is units times monomials, so the characteristic monoid is N^r. All five new nodes are true, statement-only and unsplit, with correct created/blueprint fields and four recorded searches. None restates a clause of the item. rg over the DAG (log regular, normal crossings, nodal, snc, desingularization) found no duplicate. Accepted tool uses: lem-kun-projective-implies-proper, and lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian (a Mathlib leaf, so declaring it was harmless). FIX (B3, two missing definition citations): lem-trf-log-regular-desingularization now cites def-weil-closed-immersion and def-weil-etale-morphism, and lem-trf-normal-crossings-strictification now cites def-weil-etale-morphism, inline and in stmt_deps. lean.statement: theorem exists_nodal_pair_projective_resolution (F : Type u) [Field F] [IsAlgClosed F] (Y : Scheme.{u}) [Y.Over (Spec (.of F))] [IsIntegral Y] [Smooth (Y ↘ Spec (.of F))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (.of F))] [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (.of F))] (T : Y.IdealSheafData) (hT : T.IsStrictNormalCrossingsDivisor (Y ↘ Spec (.of F))) (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X] (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsHProjective f] [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f] (η : Y) (hη : IsGenericPoint η Set.univ) [Smooth (f.fiberToSpecResidueField η)] [GeometricallyIntegral (f.fiberToSpecResidueField η)] (hfib : HasNodalGeometricFibres f) (hsmooth : ∀ x : X, f x ∉ T.support → x ∈ f.smoothLocus) (D : X.IdealSheafData) (hD : D.IsInvertible) [IsFinite (D.subschemeι ≫ f)] [Etale (D.subschemeι ≫ f)] (hmark : ∀ d : D.subscheme, D.subschemeι d ∈ f.smoothLocus) : ∃ (X' : Scheme.{u}) (r : X' ⟶ X), IsProper r ∧ IsIntegral X' ∧ Smooth (r ≫ f ≫ Y ↘ Spec (.of F)) ∧ (∃ (U : X.Opens) (V : X'.Opens) (e : V.toScheme ≅ U.toScheme), Dense (U : Set X) ∧ Dense (V : Set X') ∧ e.hom ≫ U.ι = V.ι ≫ r) ∧ ((D ⊓ T.comap f).comap r).radical.IsStrictNormalCrossingsDivisor (r ≫ f ≫ Y ↘ Spec (.of F))
